# Campaign Channel Discovery

- Discovery is operator-triggered background work, single-flighted per campaign and account; shutdown/campaign deletion cancel it. Reserve the chosen account before spawning competing Telegram work.
- A discovery account that is warming or in cooldown is not eligible; Telegram pacing/flood budget applies to every read a run makes. The exclusion is symmetric across all three runtimes: warming and the listener both refuse an account a run is reading with, and a run refuses an account either of them holds. Claim under warming's per-account lifecycle lock and re-ask BOTH owners inside it — the resolution is several awaits old by then, and the listener's generation fence cannot substitute (it is a ContextVar a task spawned from a request never sees). Health is re-read mid-run before every Telegram read, from the in-process cooldown rather than from Telegram; a limit the run did not cause stops it exactly like its own, keeps the stored candidates and is reported under its own reason.
- Every source is a Telegram read: the keyword search, the global post search (paged, narrower reach than its docs suggest), recommendations for the operator's seed, and recommendations for the sweep's own best hits. None filters by country or language, so discovery offers no locale filter at all. Subscriber bounds are applied to any source once counts are known, but never to recommendation seeds; a hit admitted with no count carries a flag, because qualification later backfills a number the bound never judged. A seed Telegram cannot resolve is a refusal, never an empty answer — otherwise it reads exactly like a good seed with no recommendations.
- A run's waves multiply reads, so they share one per-run read budget spent in wave order (keywords → the operator's seed → post pages → recommendations); the operator's explicit seed is one read and does not queue behind an automatic wave, and the recommendation wave's reads are held back before the post pages run. The post wave caps its own total, so a long keyword list buys fewer pages each rather than the whole budget. The default ceiling sits above what a run can want, so a truncated wave means the operator lowered it — truncation is reported, and is NOT a run error. The rolling-24h search allowance and per-account cooldown/flood checks are separate and unchanged. Wave shape below that one budget is a module literal, not a setting.
- Whether a read failure is a rate limit is the gateway's `kind`, never the reason text: only one member of the family spells itself FloodWait, and a non-premium account genuinely receives FLOOD_PREMIUM_WAIT. A limit with no duration takes the configured no-duration cooldown. A run also stops on `discovery_max_consecutive_errors` failed reads in a row, counted across all its waves — the qualification pass's rule, for the same reason.
- Merge interleaves per OUTCOME, not per source, before the global candidate cap: one counter per source made rank a position in the concatenation of every keyword's hits, so the first keyword filled the cap. Source priority decides dedup spelling, not which source is allowed to fill the entire cap.
- Every source reports an explicit `ran`/`failed`/`skipped` outcome, including the ones a stopped run or an empty sweep never reached. Its `hits` are the DISTINCT usable channels it returned, and everything describing the stored rows (kept, exclusive, per-row provenance, the cap flag) is only reported by a run that actually wrote — a stopped run's rows exist nowhere, and the board says the visible list is the previous search's. Replace stored candidates only when at least one source answered; an EMPTY result additionally needs the keyword sweep itself to have answered, since the always-consulted wider waves would otherwise let one empty page wipe a reviewed set. Rows any source found replace — unless a rate limit cut the run short, when the partial findings never displace the stored set.
- Qualification is resumable and stops Telegram work on any rate limit or cooldown. Do not hold the account lifecycle lock across a multi-minute discovery run.
- Per-run source progress and multi-source provenance are not persisted, so they are ephemeral across process restart; adding durability requires an explicit schema/migration decision.
- Keyword suggestion is a convenience beside the box, not part of a run: no campaign, no account, no Telegram read. It suggests single WORDS because the SPA tokenises that field on whitespace and commas, so a suggested phrase would enter it as its longest fragment — a keyword nobody proposed that then spends a real read. Both ends enforce it; the API's own per-keyword rule still allows spaces. DeepSeek only, since a campaign-less route has no Gemini secret to reach for, and an unusable answer is a 200 carrying a short code rather than a 5xx. Accepting the suggestions never starts the search: spending the read budget stays the operator's click.
